_comment: THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. It ships in the image and
install-settings.sh materialises it into <vault>/.claude/settings.json on
every agent start, so edit it here, push, deploy — never edit the copy in
the vault. A hand-edited copy is overwritten unless VAULT_SETTINGS_MANAGED=0.
README.md setup step 6, DECISIONS.md#shipping-the-tool-policy-with-the-image.
additionalDirectories adds /scratch, which is vault-research's output,
mounted here READ-ONLY. Without it every read of a research finding would
prompt on the phone: reads outside the working directory are not automatic,
and filing a topic folder is dozens of them. Listing it does not widen this
agent -- the mount is :ro in docker-compose.yml, so writes and deletes fail
at the kernel whatever this file says, and scratch-sweep.sh stays the only
thing that removes anything there.
What crosses at /scratch is material this agent did not author, which is
the same shape as the clippings already in '4. Inbox'. It is safe HERE for
the reason the whole design turns on: this surface has no way out. The
direction that must never exist is the reverse -- the vault reaching
vault-research, which has the web tools.
DECISIONS.md#a-third-surface-for-research.
MOVING FILES. Claude Code has no move tool, and Bash is denied below, so
until vault-tools existed the agent could not file a note — it could write
a copy at the new path and nothing here may delete the old one. For an
IMAGE or a PDF it could not even do that, because Write produces text and
Read cannot open one. vault-tools
is vault-mcp's binary run as a local stdio MCP server (vault-claude-mcp.json,
installed alongside this file); it serves exactly one tool and enforces the
deny list below in Go. enabledMcpjsonServers pre-approves it, because the
project-MCP trust prompt has no one to answer it in a remote-control
session. DECISIONS.md#giving-the-agent-a-move. Checked against
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp on 2026-08-30: project servers in
an .mcp.json DO prompt for approval in an interactive session, which
remote-control is, and enabledMcpjsonServers is the documented opt-in list
that skips it. The tool's permission name is mcp__<server>__<tool>.
move_file is the ONLY thing in this vault that may touch a file which is
not markdown, and it may only RELOCATE one: it creates nothing, converts
nothing, and cannot change an extension. The path denies below are NOT
relaxed for it — no dotted folder, no .mcp.json, no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md,
in either direction of the move. The movable set is attachmentExts in
../vault-mcp/vault.go: media, PDFs and canvases, never .sh/.js/.json.
HOOKS: SessionStart commits the pre-agent state; Stop commits the result.
Commits bracket agent runs via hooks rather than a timer, because a timer
can fire mid-run and capture a half-finished state. Both hooks always exit
0 — a snapshot failure must never block a session.
PostToolUse stamps the note just written with agent-created/agent-modified/
agent frontmatter, so attribution travels with the note. The snapshot repo
already records the same writes, but it is not visible from Obsidian on the
phone and a note that leaves the vault through Sync carries no history.
Per-write rather than batched at Stop, because Stop cannot tell an agent
edit from a Mac edit that Sync landed mid-session, and a wrong attribution
is worse than none. vault-mcp enforces the same three properties in
stamp.go — see the shared contract in the root README.md; the names must
not drift between the two.
PERMISSIONS: the agent reads a corpus you did not entirely author. Clipped
articles, forwarded mail and shared notes can carry instructions it will
follow. Bash and the web tools are denied because they are the exfiltration
channel that turns a prompt injection into a data breach. A notes agent
needs Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep and nothing else. See ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundary.
.mcp.json is DENIED the same way .claude/ is, and for a stronger reason:
an entry added there is an arbitrary command Claude Code will execute at
the start of every future session — the persistent compromise of the
AGENTS.md case with the shell it does not otherwise have. Note that the
deny list vault-mcp mirrors already refuses every dotted path, so the move
tool cannot be used to shuffle a .mcp.json into place either.
AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are WRITE-DENIED, at the root and nested. Claude Code
reads them as standing instructions, so an injected note that appends to one
converts a single compromised clipping into a permanent one that every future
session inherits — ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundary's 'persistent compromise, not a
one-shot'. Nested matters as much as the root: unvetted material lands in
'4. Inbox', and a CLAUDE.md there is read for work in that directory.
Reading them is still allowed; the agent needs its own instructions. Edit
these files from the Mac, never through the agent.
NOT MIRRORED HERE: vault-mcp's MCP_EXCLUDE. That server hides the folders
unvetted material lands in, because its client is claude.ai and has web
access this file cannot revoke. This agent needs to read those folders --
triaging the Inbox is most of the job -- and it is the surface that cannot
leak, because of the denies above. The two surfaces break different legs of
the same risk on purpose. Do not 'fix' the difference in either direction:
see ../vault-mcp/README.md#what-voice-cannot-see.
SYNTAX. Re-checked against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions on
2026-08-30, which now documents four path forms and settles what the
2026-08-08 note could only hedge about. The hedge was not paranoia: it was
hiding a live hole. See DECISIONS.md#the-snapshots-deny-that-was-not-one.
//path  absolute, from the filesystem root
~/path  from the home directory
/path   RELATIVE TO THE SETTINGS SOURCE -- for this file, <vault>/path
path    or ./path, relative to the current directory
So the single leading slash is the trap. Read(/snapshots/**) did not deny
/snapshots; it denied /vault/snapshots, which does not exist. Every path
here that means a real absolute path is now spelled '//'. The home
directory keeps both //home/app/** and ~/**, because those are two
different claims -- the mount, and wherever $HOME actually points -- and
the second is what was silently carrying the first until today.
Write(path) rules are ACCEPTED AND NEVER CONSULTED, and warn at startup.
They are gone from the deny list; they were decoration. What replaces them
is documented behaviour: a Read deny also blocks Edit and Write on the
same path, including creating a new file there, so the credential, snapshot,
.claude and .mcp.json paths need no write rule of their own. AGENTS.md and
CLAUDE.md are the exception that still needs an explicit Edit deny, because
they must stay READABLE -- the agent needs its own instructions -- so there
is no Read deny on them to inherit the write block from. Edit also covers
what Read cannot: NotebookEdit is outside the Read rule.
Read denies are applied to Grep and Glob against the directory their path
argument resolves to, so the deny list is not walkable with a search tool.
If you can, run /permissions in a live session and confirm each rule loaded.
